div.head: Ine 21.1
div.ab: Gyf he hit þonne dirneð, ⁊ wurð ymb long yppe, ðonne rymeð he ðam deaden to þam aþe, þæt hine moton his magas unscyldigne gedón.
Gif he hit ðonne dierneð, ⁊ weorðeð ymb long yppe, ðonne rymeð he ðam deadan to ðam aðe, þæt hine moton his mægas unsyngian.
Si celauerit, et fiat deinceps quandoque notum, tunc ampliauit mortuo ad iuramentum, quod licet parentibus suis purgare eum.
Gif he hit ðonne dierneð, ⁊ weorðeð ymb long yppe, ðonne rymeð he ðæm deaden to ðæm æðe, ðæt hine moton his mægas unsyngian.
If, however, he conceals [the killing], but it is revealed after a while, then he clears the way to the oath [being sworn] for the dead man, so that his kinsmen may prove him innocent.

If, however, he [who slew him] conceals the fact, but long afterwards it comes to light — by such conduct he affords an opportunity to the dead man to obtain an oath, by which his relatives may exculpate him.
If he [the slayer], however, conceals the deed and it is revealed long after, he opens the way to the oath for the dead man, so that his kinsmen may prove him guiltless.
Wenn er es jedoch verhehlt, und [es] wird über lang offenbar, dann räumt er dem Todten [den Weg] zum Eide, so dass diesen dessen Verwandte rein schwören dürfen.
But if he conceals it, and [it] becomes known after a long time, then he clears [the way] to the oath for the dead man, so that his kinsmen may clear him by oath.
